title: THE BED BETWEEN THEM
author: GPT

rounds.summary: The final selection contracts from a village and a star to two adjacent beds, testing whether the authorial core can sustain moral pressure without spectacle. Maren seeks a place to grieve; Halvard seeks to protect his living daughter and die without coerced confession. Illuminara's decisive understanding—that his silence is a shield and Maren is asking for burial rather than punishment—creates room for exact dialogue, restraint and love expressed as a protected exchange. The achievable result is modest but real: a verified grave, a burial, truthful speech and protection that neither party is forced to purchase with the other's destruction.
Built the complete first draft of THE BED BETWEEN THEM, with explicit goals, a falsifiable test, freely chosen cooperation and a material positive result that preserves remaining costs.

A humane, well-voiced draft with a good central instrument: a door that gives Maren a place without taking her lawful claims and gives Halvard a way to speak without being the mouth of a tribunal. Three weaknesses carry the most risk. (1) The story's own central danger, the daughter's exposure, is raised as Halvard's decisive objection and then left essentially unanswered; the positive result transfers risk to an absent person. (2) The two decisions that make the story (Halvard's concession, Maren's yes) are stated more than dramatised. (3) Illuminara's intelligence is mostly a verbal reframing of Halvard's own sentence, and the close is told in summary and omniscient report.

ACCEPTED: Halvard's danger is now exact: Corvane's surviving order book holds date, officer and burial detail but not place or dead; his own named testimony would join those records and expose Lysa. The independent parish find records place, bodies and tags without supplying his name or date. The residual risk of a later writ is stated to Halvard before he chooses, and the parish clerk names what the record does and does not prove. ACCEPTED: Both decisions now occur through visible obstacles. Maren refuses, formulates four conditions, writes a sealed identification test and retains her registry claim before consenting. Halvard hears the remaining risk and Ines's lawful limit, watches Maren commit her proof, and then voluntarily permits the single question. Ines's boundary is tested by the clerk's stated writ duty rather than left decorative. ACCEPTED: Illuminara identifies the missing evidentiary join and designs only the consent-and-information boundary; Maren, Halvard, Ines, Tobias and the clerk supply the conditions, directions, lawful limit, field proof and record. The notch sequence is sealed before the search and reported exactly before opening. The excavation, authorization, burial and closing exchange are dramatized, and the unknowable distant-daughter summary is removed.

A clear improvement on T01. The three T02 points were answered in the text rather than only in the response note: the mechanism of Halvard's danger is now exact (Corvane's book holds date, officer and burial detail but not place or dead, and his named testimony would join them), the doors now pass through visible obstacles (Maren's four conditions, Halvard's own test of the finder), Tobias and the parish clerk supply the field proof, and the closing paragraph now reports only what the ledger shows. The story is also stronger in voice and in the shared vigil. Two weaknesses are still load-bearing. (1) The safety of Lysa is claimed to follow from 'directions without a name', but the chain from the directions to Halvard (the sealed slip in Maren's hand, Ines's stated refusal to hide it from a lawful writ, the clerk's 'we answer what the law asks', and the unstated account of how Tobias came to the stone) is left open, so the improvement for the person the story itself calls the central danger is asserted more than shown. (2) Ines's confidentiality limit is again announced and never tested, and the drafts' remaining hinge, Halvard's 'Then write it', follows the clerk's reassurance more than any change in his risk that he can see.

ACCEPTED_TESTED: The public field entry now names Maren's long-running search and a private bearer, not the ward, Ninth, the date or a burial party. Illuminara alone carries the route to Tobias; the clerk keeps no second source note and can testify only to that bearer. The sealed slip contains only the pre-search tag marks, is opened after Tobias reports, signed and returned to Maren. Halvard reads this exact information topology and the remaining lawful-writ path before saying 'Ask it'. ACCEPTED_TESTED: Ines's limit is pressed directly when Halvard asks what she will say if Corvane comes. She distinguishes ordinary confidentiality from compelled truth and names the remaining cost. Illuminara's decisive perception is dramatized: she notices that Halvard reacts not to Maren's petition but to the distinction between bedside speech and public evidence, which changes the design of the field entry without taking execution away from Maren, Tobias, Ines or the clerk.

A real step forward. Both T04 points were answered in the text and not only in the response note: the public field entry now names Maren's long search and a private bearer instead of the ward, the slip is sealed and opened only after the finder reports, the clerk keeps no second note naming a source, and Halvard reads that topology and the remaining lawful-writ path before saying 'Ask it'. Ines's limit is now pressed once ('If Corvane asks whether I spoke?') and answered with a cost. Illuminara's perception is shown as an observation of where Halvard's eyes and fingers went, not as analysis alone, and the other characters still carry the execution. Outcome rule 3a is met and visible: Pell Teague identified and buried, five other dead named, Maren keeps her petition, Halvard chooses with the remaining cost inspected. Two things still weaken the piece. (1) One load-bearing premise of the protection does not quite hold on the page: the entry omits 'Ninth' to keep Corvane from finding Halvard, yet in scene 1 Maren says she has already written to the registry eleven times about the Ninth and the ford, and Halvard says Corvane has watched her search for eleven years, so 'Ninth' is not secret. The real protection is the join between a found trench and a burial DATE (the order book is by date, the burials were not), which the text states in passing but never makes the pivot. (2) The revision grew from about 2,530 to about 3,130 words, above the usual range, and nearly all of the growth is procedural: the clerk's wording is negotiated, repeated exactly and made to be repeated twice, Ines's limit is stated in scene 3, again in scene 4 and a third time as a summary line, and the closing paragraph re-explains the mechanism. The vigil, which is the story's…

ACCEPTED_TESTED: The revision makes the burial date, not the already-known Ninth, the missing join. Halvard explicitly concedes that Maren's petitions already expose the regiment; the tags and trench cannot supply the day, while Corvane's order book is indexed by date and has no burial places. The clerk's one field-page rule withholds only what the ground cannot prove. Halvard tests that exact fact before choosing. ACCEPTED_TESTED: The revision compresses procedure while preserving the chain. Ines states her limit once and answers its test once; the clerk gives the public wording once; Halvard makes one date objection; the field page is described once at the stone. The repeated wording, repeated legal summary and closing mechanism recap are removed.

Both T06 points were answered in the text, not only in the response note. P1: Halvard now concedes that the Ninth is already exposed by Maren's petitions and names the day as the missing join (tags carry marks not dates; the order book is indexed by date and holds no burial places), and the clerk's field-page wording withholds exactly what the ground cannot prove. 'No Ninth' is no longer offered as protection, so the reduced danger to Lysa is causal and checkable. P2: the procedure is compressed to roughly 2,170 words, back inside the normal range; Ines states her limit once and answers its test once, the clerk gives the public wording once, and the closing paragraph no longer re-explains the mechanism. The vigil, the 'I did not buy that promise' exchange, the three-two-one tag, the burial, the five read-aloud names and the ledger with six names above five unfinished lines (consistent with the trench: five readable, four damaged, one absent) all survive. Outcome rule 3a is met and visible: Pell is identified and buried, five other families will be told, Maren keeps her petition and a witnessed page, Halvard chooses after testing the exact fact he feared, and Illuminara's contribution (hearing where his fear was precise, and proposing a place-without-day route that Maren then conditions and Ines, Tobias and the clerk execute) is decisive without removing anyone's agency. No hard blocker. What remains is polish, not structure.
Sealed the exact source-bound final of THE BED BETWEEN THEM after the reviewed author line was complete; any same-text predecessor is preserved in the version series.

Beside a dying officer's silence and a mother who needs a grave for her son, Illuminara refuses to carry a word between them and instead listens until his fear is exact, then helps design a place-without-day route, tested in daylight with witnesses, that lets the boy be found and buried while everyone keeps the right to refuse.
